notice: Prototype field mapping from the public Intent Intelligence framework onto a partial KATA agreement. Bindings are assumed. This file does not assert compatibility with American Express.

source.title: Intent Intelligence: Building Trust in Agentic Commerce

input_schema_version.note: The pages opened on 16 October 2026 do not publish a schema version. When a sender includes schemaVersion, it is kept and reported as assumed.

bindings.note: The 13 October 2026 page describes an Intent ID as the primary key for later intent requests. It does not publish the JSON key. agreement_id is the closest KATA field.
The same Intent ID is copied onto the intent declaration so the intent object has an id. intent_id is not, by itself, the lifecycle key.
KATA mandate ids change when the signed version changes. The suffix is a draft stand-in.
Purchase Summary is a prose row on the 13 October page. No sample shows this key. KATA keeps the source sentence on natural_language_source.

Prose Max Amount has no published key. A plain decimal string is read as a major-unit number. The page does not say whether this is the per-transaction ceiling, the cumulative slice, or the sample item maxAmount. Scale was not published.
KATA restates the per-transaction ceiling on limits. This copy stays equal to maximum_amount only while both bindings read the same source.
Intent Expiry is a prose end date. No sample shows this key. When time_limit and expires_at are both set, KATA expects the same instant.
The mandate end instant is the same prose date as intent.time_limit.
The page says this count maps to payment credentials that can be issued. KATA frequency.max_count counts recorded charges. The counters differ.
The item sample shows currency as an ISO 4217 string, required when unitAmount is set. Using the first item currency as the intent currency is assumed.
The same first-item currency is copied onto limits. A mix of item currencies is not resolved here.
Merchant name is a verified sample key. Placing those names in merchant_constraints is assumed. categoryName is left on the preserved record so it is not treated as an allowlist entry.
fromDate is a verified sample key when type is DATE. Writing it to not_before is assumed. The sample does not say to do that.
toDate is a verified sample key when type is DATE. It fills expires_at only when Intent Expiry did not. The assignment is assumed.
The same toDate fills time_limit when Intent Expiry did not, so the two KATA end fields stay together.

scaffolds.note: Draft marker for an unsigned agreement. The AmEx pages do not publish this status.
No charge has been recorded. The AmEx credential log is a different object.
Lifecycle events are not invented from the AmEx record.
First draft version. An edit would be a new signed version, which this prototype does not build.
KATA requires an intent version. The AmEx pages do not publish one.
The window is not published. agreement counts across the whole mandate window. AmEx counts credentials. KATA counts recorded charges.

kata_gaps.note: The opened pages do not publish a principal key. KATA revoke accepts the signing principal.
The opened pages do not publish the agent key bound into the mandate.
Proof of Intent is described as a JWT. Header, algorithm, and claims were not published, so no KATA JWS is produced.
KATA requires a purpose. The framework page does not publish one.
No ledger sync time is present on the AmEx record.
